column5: Check the clamshell bottom for juice stains; skip boxes with mold.
column6: Grown organic first for skin-on produce and EWG's Dirty Dozen.
column7: (berries_picking) One moldy berry means spores have traveled through the whole package.

column5: Pick dark, crisp leaves; skip brown, yellow, slimy or wilted ones.
column6: Organic spinach, kale and lettuce with crisp, colorful leaves.
column7: Lettuce heads or bunches should feel heavy for their size.

column5: Bright green, dry leaves; skip yellow, limp or dark goop.
column6: ...with the USDA Organic seal, bright and upright.

column5: Plump grapes still tight on green stems; brown stems mean old.
column6: Organic, always: a Dirty Dozen fruit eaten skin-on.
column7: Plump grapes stay firmly attached to the stems.

column5: Find the 5-digit sticker code starting with 9.
column6: Organic apples and pears, firm, unbruised, unwaxed when possible.
column7: 'Unwaxed' on the sign means no coating was added to the fruit.

column5: Press near the stem with a thumb; it yields when ripe.
column6: (same card)
column7: European pears yield slightly near the stem when ripe.

column5: Choose plump fruit that gives slightly; red blush alone does not mean ripe.
column6: Organic peaches, nectarines and cherries, plump with stems on.
column7: Peaches yield gently when ripe; cherries will not ripen once picked.

column5: Firm skin with no green tint and no sprouts.
column6: Organic potatoes with good color and no sprouts or wrinkles.
column7: Skip potatoes with dark spots or wilted skin.

column5: Firm with a fresh green stem; skip wrinkles and black spots.
column6: Organic bell peppers, firm, in full red or yellow color.
column7: Red and yellow bells are green peppers left to ripen fully.

column5: Even colour, no blemishes; a bean snaps when bent.
column6: Organic green beans, slim and firm, free of soft spots.
column7: A fresh bean snaps in two rather than bending.

column5: Pick the heaviest for size; peel colour shows climate, not ripeness.
column6: Organic citrus, unwaxed when the peel gets zested.
column7: Before zesting, check the sign for a shellac-based or petroleum wax.

column5: Watermelon: yellow ground spot; cantaloupe: cream-yellow between netting.
column6: Whole watermelon with a cream ground spot and dull skin.
column7: On cantaloupe, the skin between the netting turns light tan to yellow.

column5: Smell the stem end for sweetness; ripe fruit gives gently.
column6: Whole tropical fruit, uncut, with origin on the sticker.
column7: A ripe mango gives slightly; Sugarloaf pineapple stays green even when ripe.

column5: Green for later; yellow with small brown flecks for today.
column6: Organic bananas, green-tipped for later or yellow for today.
column7: Yellow with brown spots is the fully ripe, sweetest stage.

column5: Yields to gentle palm pressure when ready; firm green needs days.
column6: Organic avocados that yield to a gentle palm squeeze.
column7: Squeeze in the palm, not with fingertips; avocados ripen only after picking.

column5: Dry papery skin and small dry neck; a damp neck means decay.
column6: Organic onions and garlic, firm, dry and papery-skinned.
column7: Garlic heads should be firm with no cuts or soft cloves.

column5: Heavy, compact heads; skip yellow florets or dry, browning stem ends.
column6: Organic broccoli, cabbage and cauliflower, compact and heavy.
column7: Cauliflower heads should be compact with no spaces between florets.

column5: Firm and smooth; skip cracked or rubbery; crisp green tops mean fresh.
column6: Organic carrots and roots, firm, smooth and bright in color.
column7: Skip carrots that are cracked, forked, limp or rubbery.

column5: Tightly closed tips; stems snap rather than bend.
column6: Asparagus with dry, closed, compact tips and no limp stalks.

column5: Green husks; silk ends free from decay.
column6: Corn with green husks and fresh silk, without dried-out ears.

column5: Closed or half-open caps with pink or tan gills; skip slime.
column6: Whole organic mushrooms with dry, springy caps.
column7: Dry brown bruises differ from wet, spreading dark patches.

column5: Uniform colour, firm, no soft spots.
column6: Organic tomatoes with plump, shiny, unwrinkled skins.
column7: A slight give when squeezed gently means ready to eat now.

column5: Firm, glossy, heavy for size, no soft spots.
column6: Unwaxed, firm, dark green cucumbers, else the USDA Organic seal.
column7: Small-to-medium, glossy and firm, heavy for size.

column5: Full, snug, vibrant green pods; skip mushy spots.
column6: Snap peas in firm, bright green pods, without blemishes.

column5: Short pods around 2 to 3 inches, tender and clean.
column6: Okra, firm and bright green, without limp, moldy or dried-out pods.

column5: Heavy, smooth, dark skin; skip shriveled or bruised.
column6: Eggplant, heavy, shiny and smooth, with a green stem free of mold.

column5: Hard intact shell, heavy for size, no soft spots or cracks.
column6: Winter squash, firm and heavy-for-size, with hard skin and no sunken or moldy spots.

column5: Solid-feeling stalks with fresh-looking leaflets.
column6: Celery with the USDA Organic seal and crisp stalks.

column5: Bright firm leaves if attached; skip cracks and brown spots.
column6: Kohlrabi bulbs, firm and heavy in your hand, without cracks or bruises.

column5: Smooth firm skin; skip dried-out, moldy or mushy areas.
column6: Ginger and turmeric roots, firm, ginger smooth and uncracked; keep both sealed and refrigerated.

column5: Pieces move freely in the bag; skip solid clumps and heavy frost.
column6: Organic frozen fruit or vegetables, single ingredient, free-flowing.
column7: Frozen fruit sometimes comes packed in syrup or added sugar.

column5: Ingredient list is the fruit alone; no added sugar.
